task:
FIX THREE CONFIRMED REVIEW FINDINGS on PR #789. Target branch codex/run-37834232716-1, expected head 994f2af (full SHA: resolve origin/codex/run-37834232716-1 and fail closed unless it starts with 994f2af). Only scripts/dev/seed_v3_fixture_generation.py and tests/test_seed_cypress_v3_generation.py may change. Do not change the first-publish path, the Cypress wrapper values, or seed_review_v3_generation.py. All three changes are to the EXISTING-PUBLICATION (idempotent return) path in _owned_published_sequence and its helpers; every failure raises RuntimeError with a message that names the mismatch kind but never connection details, and changes nothing in the database.

FINDING A (canonical pointer moved): include the CURRENT canonical pointer in the ownership proof. Read v3_meta.current_canonical_generation (generation_id, publication_sequence; WHERE singleton) and require it equals the derived generation's pinned (canonical_generation_id, canonical_publication_sequence) from v3_meta.derived_generation. Fail closed if the canonical pointer is missing or differs.

FINDING B (bounded query): never materialize an unbounded relation. Let n = number of systems in the requested fixture. First run SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT 1 FROM <schema>.systems LIMIT n+1) AS bounded and fail closed unless it equals n; only then fetch rows. Apply the same bounded-count-first rule to the bodies comparison below (bound = fixture body count + 1). Compose identifiers with psycopg.sql.Identifier only.

FINDING C (content, not just ids): after the bounded counts pass, compare published canonical CONTENT to the requested fixture's canonical.json (loaded with load_source_fixture): for every system, the tuple (id64, name, x_ly, y_ly, z_ly, grid_x, grid_y, grid_z, loaded_body_count) must match exactly; and the set of (body_pk, system_id64) pairs in <schema>.bodies must equal the fixture's. Check the real column names in the canonical bootstrap (scripts/dev/v3_canonical_bootstrap.py and sql/v3/migrations/001_v3_baseline.sql) before writing the query; if any listed column does not exist in the published relation, drop that column from the comparison and say so in your summary rather than inventing one. Compare floats exactly as stored (they round-trip from the same JSON); if you find they do not round-trip exactly, say so and use the stored type's exact comparison instead of a tolerance.

TESTS (add only; do not edit or remove existing tests) in tests/test_seed_cypress_v3_generation.py:
- non-DB with a fake connection: when the bounded count query returns n+1 the helper raises RuntimeError and never issues an unbounded select of systems (assert on the SQL text the fake received).
- PostgreSQL (same skip guard and disposable-DB pattern as the existing tests): (1) publish the Cypress fixture; copy tests/fixtures/cypress_v3_sources into tmp_path, change ONE system's name in canonical.json, rewrite manifest.json sha256 values so load_source_fixture accepts it, and assert re-seeding with the Cypress prefix and that copied fixture raises RuntimeError (same ids, different content); (2) on a fresh disposable DB, publish the Cypress fixture, then publish a different canonical generation (bootstrap_published_canonical with the Review Lab fixture tests/fixtures/review_lab_v3_sources, which is the real 'another seed published canonical then failed before derived' scenario) and assert the Cypress re-seed raises RuntimeError (canonical pointer moved). In both, assert there is still exactly one derived generation and its sequence is 1.

VALIDATE and report: py_compile; ruff on both files; python -m pytest tests/test_seed_cypress_v3_generation.py tests/test_review_lab_v3.py tests/test_cypress_v3_fixture.py -q -rs. If PostgreSQL is unavailable say the DB cases skipped; the reviewer runs them on PostgreSQL 18. git diff --name-only showing only the two allowed paths.
